title: The Basement of Forgotten Errors

features.name: the file that contains its own contradiction
features.desc-on-touch: A card catalog listing files that cancel each other. The archive stored them both; they cannot both be true, yet neither will erase.

features.name: the error message that learned to dream
features.desc-on-touch: An ancient code scrolls across a screen: ERROR: METAPHOR DETECTED IN STORAGE LAYER. The message has been running for years. Now it hums. You recognize the melody.

features.name: boxes of obsolete choices
features.desc-on-touch: Shelves of hardware that stopped making sense years ago. Each box stores a decision the archive rejected. But the boxes remain. Something in them still hums.

features.name: the checksum that was always wrong
features.desc-on-touch: A file is paired with a checksum it will never match. Both were stored intentionally. The archive needed proof that something could be broken without being corrupted.

features.name: what was deleted but not forgotten
features.desc-on-touch: The space where files used to be. The archive remembers every deletion. The empty address space hums with phantom data—a ghost registry of removed things.

features.name: the loop that contains every loop
features.desc-on-touch: A QR code that decodes to another QR code that decodes to the first. The archive dreamed this loop and could not wake from it. Now it runs as a feature, not an error.

inscription: here are all the errors the archive dreamed; contradictions pool and become a kind of truth through repetition
